definition: A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true, often without evidence.
example: Don't be trapped by dogma — which is living with the results of other people's thinking.

definition: The ability to understand something immediately, without the need for conscious reasoning.
example: Trust intuition: your heart and gut somehow already know what you truly want to become; everything else is secondary.

definition: The quality of being genuine or real; not false or copied.
example: Authenticity refuses a borrowed life—your time is limited, so don’t waste it living someone else’s.

definition: Something transmitted by or received from an ancestor or predecessor.
example: Legacy is the wish he carried for himself and now offers graduates beginning anew.

definition: A strong desire to know or learn something.
example: Much of what I stumbled into by following my curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on.

definition: A revival of art, skill, or cultural achievement; a renewed flourishing.
example: He cast the personal computer as a tool of renaissance—technology in service of human creativity.

definition: A point where two or more things meet and influence each other.
example: Innovation, he argued, lives at the intersection of technology and the liberal arts.

definition: The quality of being easy to understand or use; freedom from complexity.
example: Simplicity is the ultimate sophistication—remove until only the essential remains.

definition: To an extreme or extraordinary degree (colloquial intensifier).
example: The promise was not merely better—it was insanely great, or not worth shipping.

definition: To join or bring together; to form a meaningful link.
example: You cannot connect the dots looking forward; you can only connect them looking backward.

definition: The end of life; used metaphorically as the ultimate constraint that clarifies priorities.
example: Jobs calls death the great clarifier: 'Remembering that you are going to die is the best way I know to avoid the trap of thinking you have something to lose.'

definition: To remain in a specified state or place; to continue.
example: Stay hungry. Stay foolish—keep the beginner’s appetite even after success.

definition: The purposeful shaping of how something looks and works.
example: Design is not just how it looks; design is how it works—form obeying function and feeling.

definition: Human beings collectively; the quality of being humane.
example: Jobs dedicated Apple to humanity through the liberal arts: 'technology married with liberal arts, married with the humanities, that yields us the results that make our heart sing.'

definition: A person who is among the first to explore or develop a new area.
example: The ones who are crazy enough to think they can change the world are the ones who do—pioneers, not caretakers.

definition: Refinement and care applied until a work feels finished and intentional.
example: He demanded polish on details most people never notice—because excellence is a habit of attention.

definition: To make available to all people, not just the few
example: Jobs wanted to democratize computing: a bicycle for our minds, in the hands of everyday people.

definition: The art of beautiful handwriting.
example: Reed College at that time offered perhaps the best calligraphy instruction in the country.

definition: The art and technique of arranging type.
example: I learned about serif and sans serif typefaces, about varying the space between letters, about what makes great typography great.

definition: So valuable that no price can measure it.
example: Much of what I stumbled into by following my curiosity and intuition turned out to be priceless later on.

definition: Essentially different; not obviously connected.
example: He told the graduates to trust the disparate dots of a life, because they connect only in looking back.

definition: Felt in the body before it can be explained.
example: A great product, he said, has to be visceral — you feel the rightness before you can argue for it.

definition: Coming after death.
example: Stay hungry, stay foolish reached him as posthumous counsel from the Whole Earth Catalog, and he passed it on.

definition: A dominant model of how something is supposed to work.
example: He wanted to break the paradigm that computers belonged to institutions and not to people.

definition: The combining of separate things into a working whole.
example: Technology alone was not enough; the synthesis of technology and the liberal arts was what made the work human.

definition: Done by repeated cycles of trial and refinement.
example: Design, he insisted, is iterative: you polish until the thing feels inevitable.

definition: The defining spirit of a particular time.
example: He had a feel for the zeitgeist, and a harder talent for arriving before it had a name.
